verification_report.summary:
The full proof is correct under the stated conditional inputs. All deductions were checked in textual order, with 17 sequential audit records and four separate reference checks. No critical error or gap was found.

Conformal Gauduchon theorem: ellipticity, the maximum principle and index zero give a one-dimensional smooth real adjoint kernel. Its integral cannot vanish, since that would make Lv=1 solvable. After normalization, a negative region would likewise produce a strictly positive right-hand side orthogonal to the adjoint kernel, contradicting the maximum principle. Strict positivity is justified despite the arbitrary adjoint zeroth-order coefficient: subtracting C_+=max(C,0) leaves zeroth order min(C,0)<=0 and makes rho a nonnegative supersolution. A zero is a nonpositive interior minimum, so the strong minimum principle applies. Integration by parts and kernel dimension give the asserted equation and uniqueness.

Conserved trace and determinant bound: locally integrable quasi-psh potentials can be paired distributionally with the smooth Gauduchon test form, including when unbounded. Positivity gives a finite measure, and compact metric comparison gives the uniform positive trace bounds. The exterior-power ratios are exactly the mean and product of the Hermitian eigenvalues, so arithmetic-geometric mean gives the displayed constant and exponent. The positive-root calculation correctly inverts the cofactor relation and yields a smooth intrinsic root.

Generalized Lamari criterion: the order unit makes p finite and sublinear with p restricted to E equal to ell. Dominated Hahn-Banach gives a positive extension, and |T(Phi)|<=K ell(Gamma_0)||Phi||_C0 proves its continuity, including the case ell(Gamma_0)=0. The scalar operator D has no zeroth-order term, constant kernel and index zero; Stokes and codimension one identify its range with the integral-zero functions. Its normalized inverse gives a continuous right inverse R. Extending S composed with R by the continuous splitting zeta=(zeta-(integral zeta)Omega)+(integral zeta)Omega produces a distribution, and Phi-R(ddc Phi) in E proves exactly S=ddc u. The stipulated local characterization then supplies the canonical quasi-psh representative without requiring theta to be closed.

Quantitative threshold: every ratio has a positive denominator and lies in a common finite interval. The trace identity bounds every admissible a by kappa. Every test integral of theta-kappa omega is nonnegative, so the proved criterion applies at kappa itself and attains the largest value by a current. This also proves the stated equivalence with bigness; no minimizing smooth metric is required. Historical citations supply no premises. No bounded-mass property, positive-volume property, Kahler metric, global ddbar lemma or Monge-Ampere existence theorem is used.
